scope: Internal relay abuse review by the implementation agent; not an independent security audit
finding: When a project had 100 allocations, a new allocation was rejected before the incremented request counter was persisted. Capacity-rejected requests therefore bypassed the intended global 600-request budget.
impact: An approved integrator could continue permitted session operations after 600 total requests consisting of accepted and capacity-rejected allocations. Edge/IP throttles still applied; no unauthorized session admission or signing bypass was demonstrated.

reproduction.environment: Local Cloudflare workerd runtime; direct internal quota-object requests, no live server traffic

repair: Persist the incremented request counter even when allocation capacity rejects the request, within the same storage transaction. A full request budget still returns without additional writes.
limits: Over-budget traffic still performs quota-object lookups. This repairs admission accounting, not all infrastructure work/cost bounds; distributed load/abuse qualification remains open.
